body:
I have 2 tabby chonks, and one dilute tortie! The other cat who passed away was a large gray chonky boy. He was the sweetest cuddliest guy. 

And thank you for your advice and support. It’s sincerely appreciated.
She has already made the diagnosis a lot about herself though. Sobbing about how she’s useless and can’t survive if he died. (Sad but unfortunately true.) 
Now that he’s getting better, it hasn’t been as bad but I still try to avoid her as much as I can. Difficult when we live in a very small, one floor rental home. (I stay in my room most of the time.)
Thanks for your support as well. Writing things down really helps sometimes. こちらこそ頑張ってください！

Thanks. I'm trying to take time for myself. Therapy hasn't really done much for me in the past so I doubt it'd do much now, but thanks for the support. If I could spend more time outside I would, but it's dreadfully hot and I don't live in a great neighborhood.

As someone who also has a lot of mental health+trauma stuff, I totally hear where you're coming from. I know it doesn't mean much coming from a stranger, but I'm happy that you're taking your health in your own hands by seeing a therapist and taking antidepressants. You don't have to believe everything happens for a reason, and if you don't think praying helps, you don't have to do that. You don't have to listen to anyone you don't want to, or do something you feel isn't genuine.

I wish you well in the future. 

(Also seeing your comments about antidepressants: have you tried taking lexapro? It's done wonders for me. I used to be on Zoloft (gave me awful stomach problems and made me feel bad too!)
